audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was given to Locke in both layers while whys[4] says 'Level 6 stays even — his ult threat arrives, but without item damage he cannot reliably chunk you to threshold, so it is still a spacing war.'
audit.why: The packet chart reads Skill for Level 6 and gives Locke only the First item row. The prose already made the argument for Skill; only the side token disagreed.
audit.corrected: Level 6 flipped to Skill at 5/10 in both layers. First item left with Locke — that is the genuine Purgatory-plus-burst window and the packet agrees. Every other row already matched.

audit.why: The spike structure is right and unusually well-specified for this repo: level 6 Purgatory, the first-item burst spike, and the 2+ items recovery when Mega bulk out-survives his combo. The 'ten seconds after each spent blink' framing matches Ashen Pursuit's flat 10-second cooldown exactly, and report[7]'s 'E is his Flash, and it's on a 10-second timer' is correct.
audit.corrected: No change. I added the passive's missing-health scaling to early because it changes when a spike hurts, not which spikes exist.

audit.whatIsWrong: Purgatory's grounding is absent from every single field, in a matchup where Gnar's escape is a dash. The passive's missing-health scaling and the E auto-reset tell are also missing, and report[8].t tells the reader anti-heal is optional here.
audit.why: Purgatory grounds — Hop is a dash, so inside the zone Mini Gnar cannot leap out of the execute and has to walk. That is the mechanic that makes the first-item window lethal rather than merely scary, and it is the single most important thing on this page that was not on it. Silver Stake's on-hit damage increases with the target's missing health, so his chip accelerates exactly as you approach the execute threshold — the two effects compound. His combo opens on an Ashen Pursuit auto-reset, so the tell is a wind-up, not a cast. And Soul Ignition heals back a portion of damage taken; Grievous Wounds reduces healing regardless of whether the source is lifesteal, so 'anti-heal is optional' is the wrong read.
audit.corrected: Grounding added to whys[5], spikes[2].text and mid; missing-health scaling added to early and whys[1]; the E wind-up tell added to mid; report[8].t's anti-heal line corrected.

edits.after: Level 2 stays skill — the boomerang's return damage offsets a passive that only bites once you are low.

edits.after: First item is Locke's window — Purgatory grounds you inside the zone, so Hop cannot carry Mini Gnar clear of the execute; play this stretch in Mega or behind minions.

edits.before: Through level 5 it is an honest poke war: Boomerang return damage answers his chip, Hyper kiting matches his gap-close, and neither side has a commit button. Play the rage bar like a resource — poke in Mini, and when Mega comes up either force a Wallop trade or bank the form as insurance, because his level 6 changes what being caught low costs you.
edits.after: Through level 5 it is an honest poke war: Boomerang return damage answers his chip, Hyper kiting matches his gap-close, and neither side has a commit button. His passive scales with your missing health, so the last third of your bar costs double — reset above it. Poke in Mini, and when Mega comes up force a Wallop trade or bank the form as insurance.

edits.before: His 6-plus-first-item window is the one stretch of this lane that is genuinely his: Purgatory executes a squishy Mini Gnar caught under threshold. Respect it — stay above half HP, hug minion cover, and time Mega for when he shows engage intent. Mega with the wave shoved means he cannot touch you; Mini at 40 percent in an open lane means you are dead.
edits.after: His 6-plus-first-item window is the one stretch of this lane that is genuinely his: Purgatory executes a squishy Mini Gnar under threshold, and it grounds — inside the zone Hop is dead and you have to walk out. Stay above half HP, hug minion cover, and read the E auto-reset wind-up rather than a cast. Mini at 40 percent in an open lane means you are dead.

edits.before: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Anti-heal is optional — his sustain is self-refund, not lifesteal.
edits.after: Early HP and MR blunt the nail chip (his damage is AP). A stopwatch/Zhonya’s-class answer beats Purgatory outright: untargetable at the floor = execute denied. Grievous Wounds still cuts his W refund — that is healing like any other.

notes: This page is much better written than the rest of the champion's set and most of it survived audit. The one large gap was Purgatory's grounding: Gnar's escape is a dash, so being grounded inside the execute zone is what actually kills him, and it appeared nowhere. Ability-name caution: the full layer calls the Q 'Ritual Nails', but Riot's own Q description says 'Locke readies a set of Soul Nails to throw', and the _missing file names his other three as Silver Stake (P), Soul Ignition (W) and Ashen Pursuit (E) without ever naming the Q or R. I did not rename anything because I cannot confirm the Q's real name from the data available, and Locke does not appear in Data Dragon under a name I can cross-check. focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[1]/[3]/[5] all carry 'Ritual Nails'.
